papers.title: Recording-session scrap
lines: A hotel on State Street, one microphone and a summer of 1927 when everybody sang into it.
A woman sang with her sister-in-law. A man sang about a train. America learned its own tune.

papers.title: Note on a banjo case
lines: My grandfather's banjo came over from Africa, said the tale, as a gourd with strings.
My grandmother's tune came from Ulster. Together they made something not either, but both.

trail.clue: A pickers' tin of coins is said to lie near the old oak, 'where we met after the concert'.

papers.title: Town notice
lines: State Street runs down the middle of town, and the state line runs down the middle of State Street.
You can eat in Virginia and pay in Tennessee, and nobody has ever been arrested for it.

papers.title: Ballad sheet
lines: Barbara Allen, six verses in a Scottish accent, on a sheet printed in London in the 1700s.
Sung on a porch in the mountains, in the 1900s, by someone who had never been to Scotland.
